summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and was found to have a moderate right pleural effusion and ascites. The effusion was determined to be hepatic hydrothorax due to underlying cirrhosis. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, which improved his symptoms and reduced the effusion on follow-up imaging. His kidney function showed a mild rise in creatinine to 1.2 mg/dL, likely due to diuresis, necessitating outpatient monitoring. His home medications, including diuretics, nadolol, rifaximin, and omeprazole, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue medications, and complete outpatient lab testing to assess renal function.
